facts.raw_span: a several-week history of a progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of her right forearm
no history of trauma
no systemic symptoms
a firm, non–tender 4 × 5 cm mass was palpated in the subcutaneous tissues of the distal forearm
no overlying skin changes
Neurovascular examination of the hand was normal
Plain radiographs of the forearm showed no fracture
soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna
MRI of the right forearm revealed a mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues
the lesion was isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images
marked enhancement after gadolinium administration
cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

concepts.why: The mass arises from the bone and extends into the soft tissues, with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, which is consistent with osteosarcoma.

The lesion is isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration, which is consistent with Ewing's sarcoma.
The mass arises from the bone and extends into the soft tissues, with cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna, which is consistent with chondrosarcoma.

The firm, non-tender mass was palpated in the subcutaneous tissues of the distal forearm, with soft-tissue swelling and cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna, which is consistent with soft tissue sarcoma.
The cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement, and the soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The mass arises from the bone and extends into the soft tissues, with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, which is consistent with giant cell tumor.

rationales.F01: The progressively enlarging swelling suggests a bone or soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F04: The firm, non-tender mass is consistent with a bone or soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F08: The cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna suggests a bone tumor.
rationales.F09: The mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues is consistent with a primary bone tumor.
rationales.F12: The cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement is consistent with an aggressive bone tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: Osteosarcoma best explains the bone and soft tissue involvement with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement, and the imaging characteristics are consistent with this diagnosis.
